item.title: Chubby marmots join subscription service after sanctuary faces money trouble
item.description: In a creative twist, a biologist from Colorado turned to popular subscription service to secure funding for crucial marmot research. He shares engaging and family-oriented videos featuring yellow-bellied marmots, motivated by recent federal budget cuts affecting his long-standing project. Operating for over sixty years, this initiative not only raises awareness about marmot populations but has also begun to generate essential financial support for ongoing scientific investigations.

item.title: Part of SpaceX rocket the size of a school bus crashed into the Moon
item.description: Unexpectedly, a four-ton SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket stage has collided with the Moon, exhibiting the increasing issue of space debris. After spending over a year in orbit, the remnants triggered observable spectral lines indicative of sodium and lithium gases upon impact. NASA, alongside South Korea, intends to photograph the resulting crater to understand the event better. This incident underscores the urgency of addressing space junk management and its proper disposal.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Why wildlife managers are coating raven eggs with nontoxic oil to protect sage-grouse
item.description: A new study has found that coating common raven eggs with non-toxic mineral oil can reduce raven reproduction and improve the survival of vulnerable greater sage-grouse. Researchers reported that sage-grouse nest survival more than doubled, while their relative abundance increased by 44% in treated areas. However, they said long-term conservation also requires protecting habitat and addressing human activities that boost raven populations

item.title: Meet Marie Tharp: The woman who mapped the hidden ocean world in 1957
item.description: Marie Tharp's groundbreaking work in transforming ocean floor data into intricate maps unveiled previously unknown underwater landscapes and geological formations. Her findings prompted a reevaluation of established scientific theories about the Earth's surface, with subsequent earthquake data substantiating her revelations. Tharp's innovative cartography served as a pivotal cornerstone for the development of plate tectonics theory.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Meet Aakash Manaswi, the Florida student whose CO2 mite blower made bees healthier, increased honey across 60 hives
item.description: Aakash Manaswi has pioneered a groundbreaking technique to tackle the Varroa mite crisis threatening honey bee populations. His research indicates that carbon dioxide treatment rivals traditional pesticides in efficacy. This method stands out due to its cost-effectiveness and safety for both bees and consumers, providing beekeepers with a scalable, residue-free solution that supports honey bee conservation and enhances global food security.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: NZ councillor joins Zoom meeting from bathroom
item.description: In an unexpected twist during a televised council meeting, Dunedin City Councillor Jo Galer joined from her bathroom, laundry visible in the frame. The mayor playfully advised her to move the camera for better professionalism. To add to the intrigue, a shadowy figure emerged behind a frosted glass door during discussions on council budget, sparking viral attention online. This amusing scenario raises important discussions about maintaining boundaries while working remotely.

item.title: African Great Lakes hold 25% of Earth's freshwater as unique species face extinction
item.description: The African Great Lakes boast a treasure trove of freshwater and unique species, forming crucial ecosystems. However, they are under siege from human activities, with pollution and overfishing threatening both water quality and wildlife. This mounting pressure is exacerbated by rapid population growth and the looming specter of climate change, which further endangers the delicate balance of biodiversity in this region.

item.title: Airline ordered to pay Rs 53,923 after passenger's luggage was delivered three days late
item.description: A consumer commission ordered an airline to pay compensation for delayed luggage. The passenger's checked baggage was delayed by three days after his flight. The airline failed to provide compensation despite repeated passenger complaints. The commission directed reimbursement for essential clothing and litigation costs. This ruling highlights airline responsibilities under the Passenger Charter.
item.dc:creator: TOI Legal Desk

item.title: Scientists create world’s whitest paint that could cool buildings naturally
item.description: Scientists have created an exceptionally reflective white paint to cool buildings. This new coating bounces away nearly all incoming sunlight, reducing heat absorption. Laboratory tests show the paint reflects 98.1% of sunlight, outperforming standard paints. Outdoor trials demonstrated surface temperatures significantly cooler than ambient air. This innovation offers a practical way to lower cooling energy demand in warm climates.

item.title: Owens Backlash Over Investigation: Viral Cinema Shogun post slams her content; she pledges new updates
item.description: Candace Owens is facing renewed criticism after a viral X post accused her of dragging innocent people into her coverage of the Charlie Kirk investigation and promoting conspiracy theories. The criticism came as Owens addressed claims involving Frank Turek, saying viewers could judge his remarks for themselves, while previewing updates about Officer Bagley and Alan Robertson. The exchange has fueled fresh debate over her reporting style and the evidence behind her claims.
